articles.title: Royal Caribbean cruise ship pianist incredibly survives after plunging overboard 20 miles off California coast
articles.summary: Two Southern California fishermen spotted the man while returning from a fishing trip Friday.
articles.body:
A Royal Caribbean pianist was rescued after spending nearly nine hours treading water in the Pacific Ocean . Two Southern California fishermen spotted the man while returning from a fishing trip Friday.

Sean Norton and Grant Garrett, both of Newport Beach, were heading home from a morning of marlin fishing near Catalina Island when the boat's captain saw the man in the water around noon, nearly 20 miles off the coast, CBS LA reported .

Garrett said that when the man regained consciousness, he told them he was a pianist on the 14-deck Royal Caribbean cruise ship Ovation of the Seas.

"The only thing he said to me was, 'Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,'" Norton said, according to CBS LA.

After pulling him from the water, the crew sent out an emergency maritime call, and Newport Beach lifeguards responded to help.

"It was approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, pretty much in the middle of the ocean," Battalion Chief Adam Yacenda said, CBS LA reported.

Officials believe he may have gone overboard from the ship about nine hours before he was found.

"We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time. To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share," a Royal Caribbean Group spokesperson told The California Post in an email.

In September, Thomas Gigler, 56, was aboard the Carnival Panorama with his Michelle, when he went overboard as the ship sailed from Puerto Vallarta, Mexico, to Long Beach.

The couple, who lived in Redlands with their three sons, were reportedly celebrating their anniversary when Gigler disappeared. The computer programmer, who spent 24 years working for Esri, was presumed dead.

A passenger staying in a cabin near the Giglers told the Daily Mail that the family's accommodations were on the ship's second deck — meaning Gigler would have ascended roughly nine floors before reaching the 11th deck, where he is believed to have jumped.

articles.title: Densa camada de fumaça encobre capital da Índia; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Celebrações do Diwali, realizadas neste domingo (8), agravaram os níveis perigosamente altos de poluição de Nova Déli e sua região metropolitana.
articles.summary: Celebrações do Diwali, realizadas neste domingo (8), agravaram os níveis perigosamente altos de poluição de Nova Déli; toxidade do ar é 58 vezes maior que o limite recomendado.
articles.body:
Densa camada de fumaça em Nova Déli, na Índia — Foto: AP Photo/Manish Swarup

Uma densa camada de fumaça cobriu a capital da Índia nesta segunda-feira, após fogos de artifício iluminarem o céu de Nova Déli durante as celebrações do Diwali, agravando os níveis perigosamente altos de poluição e intensificando a crise sazonal de poluição do ar que assola a cidade todos os anos.

O ar tóxico em algumas áreas da cidade atingiu mais de 58 vezes o limite recomendado pela Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS), segundo dados de monitoramento.

Durante a manhã, quase oito horas após o principal momento dos fogos de artifício, os níveis de micropartículas PM 2.5, que podem provocar câncer, chegaram a 879 microgramas por metro cúbico na localidade de Mandir Marg, segundo a organização de monitoramento da qualidade do ar IQAir, que citou dados de uma estação do governo local.

Um turista ouvido pela agência de notícias Reuters afirmou ter se sentindo "sufocado" ao chegar à capital indiana:

"Me senti sufocado ao chegar ao aeroporto. Mal dá para ver alguma coisa à minha frente. Esperava ter uma boa vista do Portão da Índia , mas não consigo ver nada daqui. O ar está péssimo. Deveria ser agradável de manhã, com ar fresco, mas há muita poluição".

Em outubro, a Suprema Corte da Índia buscou limitar a poluição do Diwali restringindo os fogos de artifício convencionais e permitindo apenas "fogos de artifício verdes", sob condições específicas, em janelas de três horas no sábado e no domingo.

No entanto, em muitos locais, as restrições foram ignoradas e a cidade foi tomada pelos fogos.

➡️ Os fogos de artifício verdes produzem menos emissões, mas não são isentos de poluição. Eles ainda liberam partículas e outros poluentes, agravando a já perigosa qualidade do ar da cidade.

Densa fumaça encobre Nova Déli, na Índia — Foto: REUTERS/Anushree Fadnavis

Nova Déli e sua região metropolitana, lar de mais de 30 milhões de pessoas, figuram regularmente entre as áreas mais poluídas do mundo durante o inverno. A poluição se agrava porque os fogos de artifício do Diwali coincidem com o clima mais frio e com a fumaça das queimadas de resíduos agrícolas nos estados vizinhos de Punjab e Haryana.

O problema torna-se particularmente grave no final de outubro e novembro, quando as temperaturas mais baixas, a baixa velocidade do vento e as condições atmosféricas estagnadas impedem a dispersão dos poluentes. O resultado é uma densa neblina que pode persistir sobre a capital e as áreas circundantes durante dias.

Um estudo de 2024 publicado na revista científica The Lancet Planetary Health calculou que 3,8 milhões de mortes na Índia entre 2009 e 2019 estavam relacionadas à poluição do ar.

articles.title: FLIC 2026: Feira Literária de Campina Grande começa nesta segunda | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento gratuito reúne escritores e atividades culturais no Museu de Arte e Ciência e no Parque da Criança até 15 de novembro.
articles.summary: A FLIC 2026 oferece lançamentos de livros, oficinas de cordel e atividades infantis no Museu de Arte e Ciência e no Parque da Criança com entrada gratuita.
articles.body:
Feira Literária de Campina Grande 2026 tem início nesta segunda-feira (9) — Foto: Divulgação/FLIC

Começa nesta segunda-feira (9) a Feira Literária Internacional de Campina Grande (FLIC) 2026. O evento tem programação gratuita e acontece até 15 de novembro, com lançamentos de livros, rodas de diálogo, apresentações artísticas e diversas outras atividades culturais, inclusive para crianças.

A FLIC está na 9ª edição e este ano tem como tema " Campina Grande, Nordeste Imenso ", com o objetivo de valorizar a literatura e a diversidade cultural de todo o território nordestino. Entre os convidados confirmados estão Paloma Amado, filha do escritor Jorge Amado, o autor angolano Pau de Cabinda, o cantor e escritor pernambucano Lirinha e o escritor Fábio Lucas.

A programação também inclui atividades em 46 escolas de Campina Grande, com ações voltadas a estudantes. A feira colaborativa CoLaBora FLIC também está confirmada nesta edição do evento, com expositores de livros, artesanato e gastronomia. A programação inclui ainda o FLICordel, com lançamentos de livros e cordéis, oficina de xilogravura e sarau de cordelistas.

A abertura oficial do evento acontece na sexta-feira (13), no Museu de Arte e Ciência, a partir das 18h30, com lançamento da Casa FLIC e divulgação da inauguração da Casa na FLIParaíba. A programação também terá lançamentos de livros de estudantes, homenagens a professores e escritores e uma roda de diálogo com Paloma Amado, com o tema "O Nordeste Imenso de Jorge Amado e Zélia Gattai".

Já o encerramento do evento acontece no dia 15 de novembro, no Parque da Criança, das 9h às 12h, com várias ações voltadas para crianças, como experiência com xilogravura, contação de histórias, apresentações de palhaço e teatro.

articles.title: Teleférico vertical deve voltar a funcionar no PR, após duas décadas | G1
articles.standfirst: As obras de revitalização chegaram a 92% de conclusão. A reforma teve início em julho de 2025, após o teleférico vertical, localizado no Parque Estadual Vila Velha, ficar mais de duas décadas desativado.
articles.summary: As obras de revitalização chegaram a 92% de conclusão. Teleférico deve ser entregue após duas décadas desativado.
articles.body:
Parque Estadual Vila Velha vai reinaugurar teleférico vertical. — Foto: Foto: Denis Ferreira Netto/SEDEST

Após mais de duas décadas desativado, o teleférico vertical da Furna dos Andorinhões, no Parque Estadual de Vila Velha, nos Campos Gerais do Paraná, deve voltar a funcionar a partir de dezembro. As obras já chegaram a 92% de conclusão, segundo o Instituto Água e Terra (IAT), e a previsão de entrega é no próximo mês.

O teleférico — que funcionou entre a década de 1.980 e os anos 2.000 — é o único vertical da América Latina e tem uma descida de 54 metros. A atração permitirá que os visitantes caminhem por um deck flutuante que fica sobre o lago do fundo da furna.

O teleférico é conhecido como 'Elevador' e começou a ser reformado em junho de 2025, pela concessionária que administra o parque, a Soul Vila Velha, em parceria com o IAT. O investimento para revitalização foi de cerca de R$ 15 milhões, custeado integralmente pela concessionária.

A expectativa da empresa é de que a reabertura da atração aumente o número de visitantes em cerca de 50% – em 2025, 70 mil pessoas passaram pelo Parque Vila Velha.

“Estamos bastante otimistas com essa retomada e acreditamos que o equipamento contribuirá para ampliar a atratividade do parque, estimulando tanto o retorno de quem já conhece Vila Velha quanto a descoberta desse patrimônio natural por novos públicos” ,afirma o gestor executivo e diretor-presidente da Soul Vila Velha S.A., Leandro Ribas.

Neste momento, o trabalho de revitalização inclui instalação das últimas peças para a liberação do teleférico, além de testes de automação e paisagismo no entorno.

Por volta dos anos 2.000, o teleférico foi desativado devido a danos causados nos paredões de pedra da furna, que tem 450 milhões de anos. Por isso, agora as obras estão sendo acompanhadas por especialistas, segundo o IAT, seguindo medidas de proteção ambiental para reduzir os impactos sobre a fauna e a flora locais.

"A Furna dos Andorinhões abriga espécies sensíveis, e os cuidados com esse ambiente natural seguirão monitorados durante o início das operações do equipamento", informou o IAT.

Descida de 'Elevador' é de 54 metros, no Parque Vila Velha. — Foto: Foto: Denis Ferreira Netto/SEDEST

O 'Elevador' terá uma cobrança extra para quem quiser fazer a visita, além do valor de acesso ao parque. O preço do ingresso para o teleférico revitalizado ainda não foi definido.

O parque estadual fica localizado nos Campos Gerais do Paraná, e foi criado em 1953. Atualmente, ele é uma concessão do Governo do Estado do Paraná, por meio do IAT, à Soul Vila Velha, uma empresa do Grupo Soul Parques.

Teleférico fica localizado no Parque Estadual Vila Velha, nos Campos Gerais do PR — Foto: Foto: Denis Ferreira Netto/SEDEST

No parque, os visitantes podem conhecer uma trilha de arenitos, furnas e a Lagoa Dourada. Também estão disponíveis, com cobrança adicional, as atividades de aventura como tirolesa, arvorismo e cicloturismo.

Os ingressos podem ser obtidos online, pelo site do parque, ou diretamente na bilheteria, até às 15h.

articles.title: ‘Imposto do pecado’: taxistas, autistas e PCDs não pagam taxa em carro zero km; veja categorias isentas | G1
articles.standfirst: A cobrança está prevista para começar em 2 de fevereiro de 2027 e versões registradas no programa Carro Sustentável também podem ter alíquota zero se cumprirem os requisitos.
articles.summary: A cobrança está prevista para começar em 2 de fevereiro de 2027 e versões registradas no programa Carro Sustentável também podem ter alíquota zero se cumprirem os requisitos.
articles.body:
🔎 O tributo, criado pela reforma tributária sobre o consumo, começará a ser cobrado em 2 de fevereiro de 2027 e incidirá sobre produtos e atividades considerados prejudiciais à saúde ou ao meio ambiente, com o objetivo de desestimular seu consumo.

Entre os produtos sujeitos ao novo imposto estão os carros de passeio, com alíquota-base de 6,3%. Ela pode subir ou cair conforme alguns critérios . As novas regras, porém, também preveem isenção em determinados casos .

Veja os critérios abaixo para entender quais são estes casos:

O artigo 4º da medida provisória zera a alíquota-base de 6,3%, assim como qualquer adicional ou redução desse percentual, para "motoristas profissionais que destinem o automóvel à utilização na categoria de aluguel", definidos pelo texto como taxistas.

Para receber o benefício fiscal, o comprador do veículo precisa ser reconhecido pela Secretaria Especial da Receita Federal do Brasil.

A medida provisória prevê alíquota zero de Imposto Seletivo na compra de carros por pessoas com transtorno do espectro autista (TEA) que tenham o benefício reconhecido pela Receita Federal.

Mesmo antes da criação do novo tributo, pessoas com TEA já podiam comprar carros zero km com isenção do Imposto sobre Produtos Industrializados (IPI), por exemplo.

O benefício existe para esse grupo desde 2003 e, pelas regras atuais, a isenção do IPI vale para veículos de até R$ 200 mil, com intervalo mínimo de três anos entre as compras. A aquisição pode ser feita pela própria pessoa ou por seu representante legal.

Assim como nas compras feitas por pessoas com TEA, a medida provisória prevê alíquota zero de Imposto Seletivo na compra de carros por pessoas com deficiência.

Mesmo antes da criação do novo tributo, pessoas com deficiência que atendem às regras da Receita Federal já podem comprar um carro zero km de até R$ 200 mil com isenção de IPI. O benefício pode ser utilizado novamente após um intervalo mínimo de três anos.

A lista de isenções também inclui os veículos do programa Carro Sustentável, lançado pelo governo em julho de 2025 .

O benefício pode alcançar subcompactos, compactos, SUVs compactos e picapes compactas que cumpram os critérios de emissão de gases, uso de materiais recicláveis ou reutilizáveis e fabricação no Brasil.

Atualmente, essas versões já podem ter IPI zero. Para se enquadrar, o veículo deve emitir até 83 gramas de CO₂ por quilômetro, considerando todo o processo, desde a produção da energia até seu uso pelo veículo. Além disso, pelo menos 80% do peso do carro deve ser composto por materiais que possam ser reciclados ou reutilizados.

O programa também exige que etapas como soldagem, pintura, fabricação do motor e montagem sejam realizadas no Brasil.

Veja os critérios para as demais categorias

Carros de passeio que não se enquadram nas regras acima estão sujeitos à alíquota-base de 6,3%. Esse percentual pode subir ou cair de acordo com alguns critérios. Depois dos ajustes, a alíquota resultante é multiplicada por 1,21, conforme estabelecem as regras:

O primeiro critério é a fonte de energia do motor:

Alíquota do imposto do pecado por motor — Foto: arte/g1

O segundo critério é a eficiência energética do veículo . O cálculo considera um limite de energia consumida por quilômetro, que varia de acordo com o peso e a categoria do veículo.

Um carro de passeio de 1.200 kg, por exemplo, precisa consumir no máximo cerca de 1,49 megajoule por quilômetro (MJ/km) em um teste que combina percursos na cidade e na estrada para receber o desconto de 2 pontos percentuais .

Se ultrapassar esse primeiro limite, o carro ainda pode receber um desconto de 1 ponto percentual caso o consumo seja de até cerca de 1,57 MJ/km. Acima desse valor, não há desconto por eficiência energética .

O terceiro é a potência do motor, medida em quilowatts (kW) .

Desempenho estrutural e assistências ao motorista

O quarto critério avalia tanto a proteção oferecida pela estrutura do carro em uma colisão quanto os sistemas de assistência ao motorista

A redução de 1 ponto percentual acontece se um carro tem, por exemplo, controle de estabilidade, aviso de cinto afivelado, farol de rodagem diurna ou piloto automático adaptativo.

Se a versão não atender ao critério, fica sem esse desconto.

Centro Circular AutoPeças é o desmanche de carros da Stellantis, localizado em Osasco (SP) — Foto: divulgação/Stellantis

A redução é de 2 pontos percentuais quando um veículo é retirado de circulação para cada cinco carros novos produzidos. Se a proporção for de um para cada dez, o desconto cai para 1 ponto percentual.

Em ambos os casos, os carros novos considerados na contagem devem ser da mesma marca, modelo e versão.

Os carros novos também precisam cumprir metas de reaproveitamento. A partir de 2027, pelo menos 80% do peso de cada veículo deverá ser passível de reutilização ou reciclagem. Esse percentual sobe para 85% quando são consideradas também outras formas de recuperação dos materiais.

Para novos projetos, os percentuais mínimos sobem para 85% e 95% já em 2027. Em 2030, esses índices passam a valer para todos os veículos leves novos, tanto de passageiros quanto de carga.

articles.title: Grécia encontra barco com imigrantes mortos perto da ilha de Creta | G1
articles.standfirst: Cargueiro que passava pela região resgatou 18 sobreviventes e 12 mortos.
articles.summary: Cargueiro que passava pela região resgatou 18 sobreviventes e 12 mortos.
articles.body:
As autoridades gregas recuperaram 12 corpos de um barco com migrantes que navegava ao sul da ilha de Creta na manhã de segunda-feira (9), enquanto um navio cargueiro que passava pelo local resgatou 18 pessoas da mesma embarcação, informou a guarda costeira.

Não havia informações adicionais disponíveis de imediato sobre a identidade das 12 pessoas que morreram, nem sobre as circunstâncias de suas mortes. A guarda costeira grega informou que a embarcação em que viajavam foi encontrada a cerca de 15 milhas náuticas — aproximadamente 28 quilômetros ou 18 milhas — ao sul da ilha de Creta, no sul do país, na manhã de segunda-feira.

Outras duas embarcações, uma com 47 pessoas a bordo e outra com 40, também foram encontradas navegando ao sul de Creta. A guarda costeira informou que todos estavam sendo levados para um porto na costa sul de Creta.

Nos últimos meses, milhares de migrantes têm feito a perigosa travessia marítima desde a costa norte da África até a Grécia. A Grécia está localizada em uma das rotas mais utilizadas por pessoas que fogem de conflitos e da pobreza na África, no Oriente Médio e na Ásia, em direção à Europa.

articles.title: Newspaper headlines: 'There are more like Brand' and 'Steep cuts to EV targets'
articles.summary: A minister warns "there are more like [Russell] Brand" and the government plans "cuts to EV targets" - some of Monday's headlines.
articles.body:
According to the Sun , Russell Brand has moved almost £9m out of one of his companies, which could stop money going to his victims. The Metro says Brand, who will be sentenced for rape and sexual assault on Monday, has transferred ownership of a £5m mansion to his wife. The Daily Mirror focuses on comments from Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy who warned the entertainment industry was not "doing enough" to protect women. "There are more like Brand" reads its headline.

The Times leads on its interview with a senior military commander, who says "hunt forces" are being sent overseas to disrupt hackers preparing to attack Britain's military systems. Major General Mike Fayers, the head of the Defence, Cyber and Electromagnetic Force, confirms to the paper that missions are already under way.

The i Paper front page says ministers have been warned that the UK's rail network is at risk from a major cyber attack, that could cost the economy almost £2bn. It says Department for Transport documents have set out plans to bolster resilience against such threats.

The Guardian leads on government plans to reduce electric vehicle targets. The paper notes the move will alarm Labour MPs already worried about ministers' commitment to the green agenda. Downing Street tells the paper that the government is united in its commitment to the zero emission vehicle mandate and no decisions have been made.

After taking control of Congress in the US midterm elections, the Democrats have reiterated their intention to impeach close aides of President Donald Trump, according to the Financial Times . The report says the defence secretary, Pete Hegseth, Elon Musk's purge of federal employees and donations made by businesses to Trump's ballroom could all be investigated.

The Daily Telegraph focuses on calls from the former prime minister Lord Cameron for drugs proven to slow Alzheimer's to be made available on the NHS. The paper says he has joined a number of leading specialists in demanding an end to the block on the treatments through the health service. A government spokesman says two drugs are currently being evaluated by The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence.

articles.title: '3-month North India tour': How Bengaluru serial killer forced boy to send voice messages to conceal parents' murder
articles.summary: BENGALURU: For five days after his parents went missing, the 10-year-old son of the murdered couple Shankar and Nalini was made to tell relatives and
articles.body: BENGALURU: For five days after his parents went missing, the 10-year-old son of the murdered couple Shankar and Nalini was made to tell relatives and family friends that they were away on a pilgrimage and later on a three-month North India tour.The messages were not his own.Police said the boy told them that alleged killer Indushekhar dictated what he should say and made him record voice messages using mobile phones belonging to his parents and others.According to the boy's statement, his father went missing on a Saturday morning, and his mother was nowhere to be found by afternoon. Indushekhar came to pick him up that evening, saying they would go on a pilgrimage.Police said the child trusted Indushekhar because he was a familiar person and had ties with the family. The boy told them that Indushekhar did not allow him to speak directly to relatives.Instead, he handed him the phones and made him record voice messages. Initially, he was instructed to say his parents were at a temple and had handed their phones to people there."He told me to say they were going on a North India tour for three more months and no one should bother them," police quoted the boy as having said.The child also recalled a foul smell inside Indushekhar's car during the period. The boy noticed two or three heavy gunny bags in the vehicle and asked the accused about the stench. Indushekhar allegedly dismissed his questions, saying there were waste materials in the back.When he tried to look inside the bags, Indushekhar allegedly scolded him and warned him against going near them. articles.title: A cleaner became a stamp collector's closest companion, inherited most of his £250,000 estate and bought his disputed £200,000 stamp collection for £1
articles.summary: A job advertised as household cleaning gradually developed into something quite different for Sue Pope.
articles.body: A job advertised as household cleaning gradually developed into something quite different for Sue Pope. What began as paid work at the home of elderly stamp collector Ray Watts eventually involved looking after his daily needs, accompanying him to stamp fairs and helping with aspects of his personal life. By the time Watts died aged 90 in 2021, Pope had become one of the most significant people in his life. He had changed his will, leaving her most of his estate, while also selling her his stamp collection for a nominal sum of £1. The decision, however, became the subject of a family inheritance dispute.How a cleaner became an important part of the stamp collector’s lifeWatts, a former Lloyds Bank clerk, had spent much of his later life collecting and dealing in stamps. His interest in philately became a major part of his routine, with his collection eventually containing items dating back to the 1840s.Pope entered his life after responding to an advertisement for a cleaner. Her responsibilities gradually expanded beyond domestic work, and she began helping him with everyday tasks and personal care. She also accompanied him to stamp fairs and became involved in other parts of his routine.According to evidence presented during the inheritance proceedings, the relationship had developed considerably by 2015. Pope's representatives argued that her involvement went well beyond what would ordinarily be expected of someone employed to clean a house.She described herself as more than a cleaner and informal carer, maintaining that she had become an important companion to Watts during his later years. That closeness would eventually become central to the disagreement over his estate.How his family became part of his £250,000 inheritance plansWatts had two marriages and a blended family. With his first wife, Madeline Watts, he had three children: Nicholas, Lesley and Deborah. Madeline died in 1995. As reported by The Sun, in 1998, he married Fay Watts, who had three children from an earlier relationship: Beverley Neate, Mark Brennan and Sean Brennan. Fay died in 2011, leaving Watts with a family that included three biological children and three stepchildren.A will drawn up in 2007 reflected that family arrangement. It provided for his estate, including his share of the family property in Great Waldingfield, near Sudbury in Suffolk, to be divided equally among the six children and stepchildren.A 2019 will left most of his £250,000 estate to his cleanerIn 2019, Watts was admitted to hospital after suffering a serious fall at home. He had reportedly remained on the floor for several hours before being discovered. During this period, arrangements were made for a new will. Rather than distributing his estate equally among all six family members, the revised document provided £15,000 each for his three biological children and Neate.The remainder was left to Pope. The estate was estimated to be worth approximately £250,000, with Watts' share of the family home forming part of the assets. The changes did not end there. In 2020, another legal document, known as a codicil, was drawn up to amend the existing will. This reduced Neate's inheritance from £15,000 to just £1.The £200,000 stamp collection was sold to Pope for £1Alongside the inheritance, Watts' stamp collection became another important part of the dispute. The collection was particularly valuable because of its age and the number of historic items it contained. Neate estimated the collection's value at approximately £200,000, with some stamps dating back to the 1840s. Pope disputed that figure, putting its value at around £40,000.Watts had sold the collection to Pope for just £1, a nominal payment that added another dimension to the disagreement between the parties.The transaction meant Pope stood to receive not only the majority of an estate valued at about £250,000 but also a collection whose potential market value was disputed. The difference between the two valuations became part of the wider family argument over the arrangements made before Watts' death.His stepdaughter questioned whether he understood the new arrangementsNeate subsequently challenged the 2019 will and the 2020 codicil at Central London County Court. Her case centred on whether Watts had fully understood and approved the documents that changed the distribution of his estate. Her legal team questioned his mental condition around the time the new will was prepared. They referred to his hospital admission and argued that he had been experiencing confusion, reduced consciousness and a slowing of his thought processes.Barrister Nathan Wells, representing Neate, also raised concerns about Pope's involvement in the arrangements. He argued that the cleaner had a substantial interest in the outcome and had played a significant part in bringing solicitors to meet Watts in hospital.The legal challenge pointed to the contrast between the 2007 will and the later documents. A sudden change in the distribution of an estate, particularly when the main beneficiary is closely involved in the testator's care, can raise questions about whether the person making the will understood its contents and made the decision independently. Neate's representatives maintained that the circumstances surrounding the documents required closer examination. They also argued that leaving her just £1 was inconsistent with the relationship she believed she had maintained with her stepfather.She told the court that they had remained in contact over the years. She had helped him attend medical appointments, and he had spent Christmas with her and her husband.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘Task Force Iron Gate in full force' to choke Iran's trade routes, says Donald Trump
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Sunday announced that ‘Task Force Iron Gate’ was operational against Iran, claiming that the US naval blockade had severely
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Sunday announced that ‘Task Force Iron Gate’ was operational against Iran, claiming that the US naval blockade had severely restricted the movement of goods into and out of the country.Taking to Truth Social, Trump said, “Task Force Iron Gate is in full force and effect in the Islamic Republic of Iran. Coupled with history’s greatest Naval Blockade, very little gets into, or out of, Iran!”The announcement came even as Trump signalled that fresh US military strikes on Iran were unlikely if diplomatic negotiations made progress. He said it was “highly unlikely” that further attacks would be necessary if Tehran agreed to a “very strong agreement” covering its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Speaking to CNN, he said further military action was unlikely if negotiations progressed, but warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if strikes resumed.“I would, if necessary, but we hit them really hard,” Trump said, adding that the US had already significantly weakened Iran's military and economic capabilities.What is Task Force Iron Gate?Task Force Iron Gate is a newly established US initiative aimed at disrupting Iran's overland supply and trade routes. Ordered by US Central Command (CENTCOM) chief Admiral Brad Cooper on Saturday, it will comprise around 20 civilian and military personnel based in Tampa, Florida.The task force will coordinate with other US government agencies to prevent the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and illicit revenue across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. It is an inter-agency coordination initiative, rather than a newly announced combat deployment.The initiative expands Washington's existing naval blockade, announced in July, which targets Iranian ports along the Arabian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman. CENTCOM said the blockade had prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion worth of crude oil in recent months. Humanitarian aid is exempt from the restrictions.While the naval blockade focuses on maritime trade, Iron Gate is intended to extend restrictions to land-based supply networks and routes through the Caspian Sea.You use AI every day. articles.title: Cruise ship pianist rescued from sea after nine hours in Pacific Ocean
articles.summary: Two US fishermen say they spotted the man treading water around 20 miles (32km) off the Californian coast.
articles.body:
A cruise ship pianist was found treading water around 20 miles (32km) off the Californian coast after falling overboard, according to US media reports.

Two fishermen discovered the Royal Caribbean employee near Catalina Island on Friday and officials believe he may have been in the Pacific Ocean for nine hours, according to CBS News, the BBC's US news partner.

"I'm like, 'Yeah, it's a human being. Stop the boat; let's get all of our lines in," Grant Garrett was quoted as saying, recalling the moment he and Sean Norton spotted him.

The man, who has not yet been identified, was taken to hospital in a stable condition, the US Coast Guard told the BBC, adding it was investigating the incident.

The fishermen say the man identified himself as a pianist on a 14-deck cruise ship called the Ovation of the Seas.

"The only thing he said to me was, 'Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,'" Norton said.

The Coast Guard said in a statement it had received a report from "a Good Samaritan who recovered a conscious individual from the water".

The person was handed over to Newport Beach Lifeguards, who confirmed he was an employee of the Ovation of the Seas cruise ship, it said.

Lifeguard officials believe he may have fallen overboard at around 02:30, about nine hours before he was discovered.

"It was approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, pretty much in the middle of the ocean," Newport Beach Lifeguard Battalion Chief Adam Yacenda told CBS.

Norton credited the man's survival to unusually warm ocean temperatures.

"You have this crazy super El Niño year. This guy was in the water for probably 10 hours, but the water's 76 degrees," Norton said, which equates to about 24C.

"A different year, no way he makes it," Norton said.

The developing El Niño climate phenomenon is now the strongest on record, according to scientists monitoring the Pacific, with ocean temperatures about 3.05C above average.

In a statement to the BBC, a Royal Caribbean Group spokesperson said: "We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time.

"To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share."

articles.title: Chancellor Merz backs Ilse Aigner as Germany's first female President
articles.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has backed Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner as his preferred candidate for the country’s presidency, bringing her closer
articles.body: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has backed Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner as his preferred candidate for the country’s presidency, bringing her closer to becoming Germany’s first woman head of state.Merz conveyed his support for Aigner, 61, at a dinner hosted by his Christian Democratic Union (CDU) in Berlin on Sunday, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. The chancellor, who also leads the CDU, is expected to make his endorsement official on Monday, the person said.The move follows pressure on Merz from within his party after he failed to put forward a CDU candidate. He had initially held back from supporting Aigner, whose candidature was promoted by Markus Soeder, leader of the Christian Social Union (CSU), the CDU’s Bavarian sister party.Merz and Aigner share close personal ties and frequently meet in her constituency in Bavaria, where the chancellor has a holiday home, an official said, Bloomberg reported.Aigner has support across party lines, including among conservatives, Social Democrats and Greens. The Social Democrats, who are part of Merz’s coalition government, indicated their backing last week, according to a party official. The Greens have also signalled support in recent days.Who is Ilse Aigner?Aigner is the speaker of the Bavarian state parliament. She has held ministerial positions in two governments led by former chancellor Angela Merkel. She returned to Bavaria in 2013, having earlier trained as an electrician and worked on developing electrical systems for helicopters before entering politics in the 1990s.Her election would mark a first for the CSU, which has never had one of its members serve as Germany’s head of state. Previous conservative presidents have all belonged to the CDU.Although the CDU and CSU operate as separate parties in their respective strongholds, they contest national elections together and share a parliamentary group in the Bundestag.What does the German president do?Germany’s president occupies a largely ceremonial position and remains separate from the day-to-day political contest. However, the office-holder also serves as a symbolic figure and is regarded as the country’s moral conscience.Aigner would succeed Frank-Walter Steinmeier, 70, a Social Democrat and former foreign minister who unsuccessfully challenged Merkel for the chancellorship in 2009.Steinmeier cannot seek another term after completing two five-year stints. His presidency is due to end on March 18.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Who is Alice Huang? Chinese businesswoman at centre of Nvidia spy scandal
articles.summary: Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman accused by US intelligence agencies of working for Beijing, has emerged at the centre of a major controversy
articles.body: Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman accused by US intelligence agencies of working for Beijing, has emerged at the centre of a major controversy involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. According to a report by The New York Times, China's Ministry of State Security recruited Alice Huang to gather intelligence on the chipmaker's chief executive and potentially influence the company's decisions on advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chip sales to China.The allegations have prompted Nvidia's board to launch an independent investigation after reports that Jensen Huang, 63, had developed a close relationship with the businesswoman. The Nvidia chief has separately admitted to being unfaithful to his wife and apologised to his family and colleagues. However, the company has maintained that it has no reason to believe its trade secrets or US national security were compromised.From television reporter to a top executive at MegaspeedAlice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese citizen who previously worked as a television reporter in China before moving into the technology and business sector. She eventually became a senior executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a data centre company that provides AI computing infrastructure to businesses, including major Chinese technology firms.According to The New York Times, Megaspeed began making multibillion-dollar purchases of advanced Nvidia chips around 2024. The company reportedly bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia processors over two years, making it one of the chipmaker's biggest customers in Southeast Asia.Huang is also understood to have developed connections with senior executives across the AI chip industry. She attended technology conferences and private business dinners and had professional links with leaders at companies involved in assembling Nvidia-powered supercomputers.The New York Times reported that US intelligence agencies had monitored her communications for at least a year before concluding that she was working for China's Ministry of State Security (MSS). A classified intelligence assessment circulated among senior Trump administration officials reportedly identified her as an asset recruited to collect information on Jensen Huang.US intelligence agencies determined that Alice Huang, pictured drinking whiskey and dining with the tech mogul, was secretly passing information to Beijing, the newspaper reported.The report also said electronic surveillance identified Jensen Huang as one of her contacts. The two are not related.Intelligence operation and Megaspeed's China linksAccording to the intelligence assessment cited by The New York Times, Beijing's objective was potentially to gain insights into Nvidia's operations and influence its position on allowing China access to advanced AI processors.Megaspeed's business model has also come under scrutiny. The company reportedly built data centres across Southeast Asia and rented computing power to Chinese technology firms, including Alibaba. This arrangement could potentially provide Chinese companies access to advanced Nvidia chips despite US restrictions on direct sales to China.US authorities have also examined whether Megaspeed helped Chinese companies circumvent export restrictions. The New York Times reported that the network of businesses and investors connected to Huang had links to companies in Shanghai and Zhejiang, as well as financial connections to China's military technology establishment.Alice Huang has not publicly responded to the allegations or multiple requests for comment. Megaspeed has said its current leadership takes the claims seriously and has appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation.Nvidia, meanwhile, has defended Jensen Huang's interactions with the businesswoman, describing them as normal customer engagements. A company spokesperson said the CEO regularly meets thousands of customer executives and that such interactions do not involve sensitive trade secrets.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week
articles.summary: New petrol or diesel cars are due to be phased out by 2030 and by 2035 all new cars must be zero emission.
articles.body:
The UK government's electric vehicle (EV) targets are expected to be reduced this week in a move likely to be welcomed by carmakers but opposed by environmental groups.

Under the current rules, 80% of new cars sold in the UK must be electric by 2030 but industry groups have long called for "urgent relief".

New petrol or diesel cars are due to be phased out by 2030 and by 2035 all new cars must be zero emission.

But the speed of the transition to electric has been hotly debated, including within the cabinet.

The government has been consulting on reducing its 80% rule and a significant reduction is now expected.

Downing Street has insisted no decision has been made.

A government source told the BBC it would approach the issue in a "pragmatic and balanced" way.

If ministers do decide on a steeper watering-down of the rules, it will arguably be interpreted by some - alongside the approval of the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea - as the government prioritising economic considerations over environmental ones.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has recused himself from this issue due to his wife's links to an electric vehicle company.

The key meetings on the subject will instead be chaired by Cabinet Office minister Louise Haigh.

Sustainability groups say any weakening of the 2030 target will threaten the UK's long-term electrification and climate goals.

It could undermine the UK's claim to be providing leadership on climate just as ministers head to Turkey for COP31, the UN's climate summit.

Energy UK, the trade association for the energy industry, has also opposed the move.

Last month, it said reducing targets could damage "the investment certainty needed to deliver the infrastructure, innovation and services required for the transition to zero-emission transport".

Asked if climate change was no longer a big priority, Health Minister Karin Smyth said the government was committed to its emissions targets.

"This country is doing great work in terms of our transition and looking at renewables – that's a key part of growth in different parts of the country," she told BBC Breakfast.

She added that the prime minister would have "a good story to tell" when meeting other leaders at COP31.

A government spokesperson said: "We are committed to the phase out of all new cars relying solely on petrol and diesel engines by 2030, and to 100% of new car and van sales being zero emission by 2035, and our legally binding net zero targets."

UK electric car sales target set to be weakened

Electric vehicle sales targets could be cut after pressure from car makers

EU waters down plans to end new petrol and diesel car sales by 2035

Net zero means balancing the amount of planet-warming "greenhouse" gases produced by human activities with the amount being actively removed from the atmosphere.

The government's policy to phase out petrol and diesel vehicle sales has undergone multiple changes since it was first introduced by former Prime Minister Boris Johnson in 2020.

His successor Rishi Sunak pushed back the timeline to 2035, and the Burnham government set up a review of the EV sales targets in August.

Sunak introduced phased targets for EV sales in the UK, known as the Zero Emission Vehicles (ZEV) mandate.

Under the ZEV mandate, the percentage of new car sales that need to be EVs increases each year. The target was 28% for 2025, 33% for 2026, and so on until it reaches 80% by 2030.

Pressure in the European Union saw the bloc scrap a similar plan to ban new petrol and diesel car sales by 2035, particularly from countries with large auto industries such as Germany.

The Conservative Party has also vowed to abandon the petrol car ban if it wins the next election, with leader Kemi Badenoch calling it a "well-meaning, but ultimately destructive piece of legislation".

Green Party leader Zack Polanski said the government was "building up a shocking record of backsliding and bad decisions on climate issues".

articles.title: David Geffen, a $55-a-week William Morris mailroom clerk in New York, said he made $2 million within five years of joining the agency
articles.summary: Discover how David Geffen transitioned from a mailroom clerk at William Morris Agency to earning $2 million in just five years through strategic moves in the music publishing industry.
articles.body: In 1964, David Geffen joined the mailroom of William Morris Agency in New York. He was 21 years old and was earning $55 a week. Geffen had reportedly found this job after trying several jobs in the entertainment industry following his college dropout. While the position in the mailroom was not glamorous, it placed him inside one of the industry’s influential talent agencies. There, he could observe and learn how agents negotiated deals and built relationships with artists. In an interview with David Sheff in 1994, Geffen recalled that five years after entering the entertainment agency, he had transitioned into an independent agent and made $2 million through a music-publishing deal involving singer-songwriter Laura Nyro. The money wasn't from his salary at William Morris; it came from selling his interest in Nyro’s publishing catalogue.He had recognised the opportunity immediately. Geffen recalled that as he delivered correspondence to agents’ offices, he listened to their phone conversations and noted how they negotiated with the clients and industry executives. He realised soon enough that the work here depended on persuasion, contacts and the ability to recognise artists with potential. In his interview with Sheff, he shared that while listening to those conversations, he realised that it was something that he could do as well. He also admitted that he had claimed to be a UCLA graduate on his application, although he had not completed a degree there. In the interview, he shared that to prevent the company from discovering his false claim, he reached the office early every day while he was still working in the mailroom and went through every single piece of mail that came into the agency, looking for the letter from UCLA.From William Morris mailroom to becoming an agentGeffen was born in Brooklyn, New York and had struggled academically. He even attended more than one college without completing his studies. Prior to joining William Morris, he worked as an usher at CBS Television Studios in Hollywood. Following that, he even had a stint as a receptionist at a production company. Those jobs served as an introduction to the entertainment business, but he wished for a role that brought him closer to making decisions. He eventually contacted William Morris and secured a mailroom position in 1964.His progress at the agency, however, was not an uninterrupted promotion. In 1965, after discovering a competitor’s client list that had originally been sent to his supervisor, Geffen took it to the head of the New York office. His supervisor sacked him, but the agency’s senior management rehired him and promoted him to an assistant position. Later on, Geffen started helping an agent recruit new clients. By 1966, he had become an agent in the television department.Laura Nyro and the $2 million publishing dealGeffen’s move into music management brought him into contact with Laura Nyro, a singer-songwriter whose career had met a setback after a challenging show at the 1967 Monterey Pop Festival. He became her agent and manager. As he started working for Nyro, he reportedly also became involved in her publishing business, Tuna Fish Music. Geffen secured a 50% interest in the company. The value of the publishing catalogue increased with the attraction from other performers and recordings of Nyro’s compositions.However, this arrangement became entangled in a legal dispute that involved Nyro’s past contracts with manager and publisher Artie Mogull. The PBS timeline notes that an agreement to sell Tuna Fish Music was reached in 1969, while the formal paperwork was completed in 1971 after the dispute reached a settlement. While speaking to Sheff in 1994, Geffen shared a more compressed account. Recalling the period around the 1969 Woodstock festival, he said he had already made $2 million. He shared that he owned half of Nyro’s publishing rights and that the catalogue was sold for $4 million, thus giving him $2 million.From representing artists to building record labelsThe publishing deal gave Geffen financial freedom, though his next move came with a separate challenge. While managing Jackson Browne, he struggled to persuade established record companies to sign his client. Atlantic Records chief Ahmet Ertegun reportedly suggested that if he believed in Browne’s potential, he should consider establishing a record company and record him himself. Geffen paid heed to that advice and launched Asylum Records in 1971.Asylum became an important part of Geffen’s move from talent agent to music ownership. In 1972, he sold the company to Warner Communications for $7 million. After a period away from the record business, he returned in 1980 and established Geffen Records. His new company represented artists like John Lennon and Yoko Ono, Elton John, Donna Summer, Aerosmith and Guns N’ Roses.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1943, U.S. Navy Lieutenant John F. Kennedy carved a rescue message into a coconut shell after his PT boat sank; it helped save 11 crewmen, and he kept it as a paperweight
articles.summary: Discover the incredible story of how U.S. Navy Lieutenant John F. Kennedy used a coconut shell to rescue his crew after his PT boat sank during World War II. This fascinating tale highlights Kennedy's bravery and resourcefulness and the unique role that a coconut played in saving 11 lives.
articles.body: A small coconut shell became an unusual reminder of one of the most difficult experiences in John F. Kennedy‘s World War II days. Before becoming the 35th President of the United States, Kennedy was a US Navy officer who operated in the Pacific during World War II. In August 1943, his patrol torpedo boat was hit by a Japanese destroyer, causing him and his men to be stuck in the water. As help seemed impossible, Kennedy and his men needed to come up with something in order to reach the Allies. A man from the nearby island suggested that they use a coconut husk for writing the message. Kennedy wrote their story on the coconut and it was delivered to the Allies by two Solomon islanders. All 11 survivors, Kennedy included, were rescued, thanks to the coconut. Later on, Kennedy placed the coconut in a wooden and plastic holder and used it as a paperweight in his office.Japanese destroyer Amagiri rammed PT-109Kennedy took command of the motor torpedo boat PT-109 on April 23, 1943, according to the U.S. Navy History and Heritage Command. The boat served in the Solomon Islands, where the US forces aimed to prevent Japanese vessels from delivering supplies to the Japanese soldiers in the area. Such an operation carried out by the Japanese was called the Tokyo Express. During the night of August 1-2, PT-109, along with 14 other American patrol boats, patrolled in the Blackett Strait to attack Japanese destroyers.At about 2:30 AM, the Japanese destroyer Amagiri approached PT-109. At first, Kennedy failed to recognise the approaching ship due to darkness. However, he attempted to maneuver PT-109 so that it could shoot the Japanese destroyer. However, there was not enough time for that. The destroyer collided with PT-109 and destroyed the wooden boat. The collision sent the entire crew into the water and ignited the gasoline that had spilled all over the wreckage. Two members of the crew, Andrew Kirksey and Harold Marney, went missing and were believed dead. The remaining 11 men survived and managed to reach the floating wreckage.It was Kennedy who managed to gather all the living men and organised their escape to safety. There was one crew member, Patrick H. McMahon, who was badly burnt and unable to swim. While McMahon was hanging onto his life jacket strap, Kennedy towed him through the water. Finally, they arrived at a small island.Kennedy and his crew struggled to contact Allied forcesThe first stop of the survivors was Plum Island or Bird Island. Later on, they went to Olasana Island, where they looked for food and water. There were also attempts by Kennedy and another officer named George Ross to look for any American patrols that might have passed through Ferguson Passage; however, their search yielded no results. On August 5, Kennedy and Ross finally arrived at Naru or Cross Island. Here, they found some supplies and a canoe. At this point, they also met Solomon islanders named Biuku Gasa and Eroni Kumana, who worked as scouts for the Allies.At first, the islanders were quite wary about meeting the Americans. However, with the help of another surviving officer, Lt. Leonard Thom, they convinced the two islanders that they were Americans and needed their help. The next day, August 6, Kennedy went back to Naru with the two Solomon islanders. To get word of the sailors’ whereabouts to the coastwatchers, he needed a way to send it. Gasa suggested writing a message on the Green coconut husk.The coconut carried a message, confirming that 11 men were aliveKennedy put a note on the shell of the coconut. This note gave information regarding the exact location, stated that there were 11 men still alive, and that there was a man who would help in navigating a boat around the area. The note said, “NAURO ISL… COMMANDER… NATIVE KNOWS POS’IT… HE CAN PILOT… 11 ALIVE… NEED SMALL BOAT… KENNEDY.”Gasa and Kumana delivered the coconut to the coastwatchers from the Allied side. Lieutenant A. Reginald Evans, who happened to be posted in the area, received the message. The message gave the coastwatchers the information they needed. According to the National Archives article “Sixty Years Later, the Story of PT-109 Still Captivates,” Gasa suggested using a green coconut husk; the two islanders delivered Kennedy’s message and Kennedy and Ross had earlier tried and failed to find American patrol boats.Allied forces rescued the surviving crewOn the morning of August 7, eight islanders came to Naru with food and instructions from Evans. Evans wanted Kennedy brought to his station so he could organise the rescue. The islanders hid Kennedy under palm leaves and took him to Gomu Island. Kennedy talked with Evans and found out that the rescue operation was being organised. He assured Evans that he would lead the American patrol boats safely through the area’s coral reefs and shallow waters to avoid any grounding.Later on August 7, Kennedy joined the crew of PT-157. He helped guide PT-157 and PT-171 through Blackett Strait to Olasana Island, where the other crew members were waiting. The rescue occurred early on August 8. All 11 survivors made their way to Rendova by 5:30 AM, six days after the accident. Kennedy was awarded the Navy and Marine Corps Medal for his bravery and resourcefulness in the situation and he later received the Purple Heart for his injuries.Kennedy kept the coconut as a paperweight in the Oval OfficeThe coconut message stayed with him, even after being rescued. Later on, Kennedy preserved the coconut shell inside a wood and plastic case, which was used as his paperweight on his desk at the Oval Office when he was the President. This was his own memento of the events that happened in 1943 with the help of Gasa and Kumana. The National Park Service’s account of Kennedy‘s World War II service includes a photograph of the preserved coconut and confirms that he used it as a paperweight in the Oval Office.You use AI every day. articles.title: Inside the French drug gangs recruiting children to kill
articles.summary: The BBC enters Marseille's dangerous underworld, where young people are trapped, brutalised and exploited.
articles.body:
Warning: Strong language and descriptions of sexual violence

It was because, along with the illegal drugs, she had been handed a note by the young seller during their brief meeting on a Marseille housing estate in 2022.

"We're being held captive and need help. We are 15-years-old," it read.

The teenage dealer, a French court heard earlier this year, was one of two boys being held by a gang which they had both initially approached looking for paid work - albeit illegal.

One boy had been tasked with handling money, the other worked streets around the Frais-Vallon estate. Soon though, bosses had accused them of being responsible for "shortfalls" in takings.

What followed were regular beatings, the court was told, and being forced to dance naked in front of a camera as a form of blackmail. One of the boys was also raped.

Hours after the woman was passed the note, the two teenagers had tried to escape from a second-storey window, injuring themselves in the process. One managed to get away, while the other was caught, beaten and stabbed, but survived.

Arrests were made. Photos on the phone of one of the boys' alleged torturers showed several other young men in a similarly distressed condition. Six men have since been handed hefty sentences for what happened to the two teenagers.

The boys' story highlights the grip that drug gangs hold over parts of France's second city.

While the blend of Mediterranean culture, street art and hip-hop scene has made Marseille a popular tourist destination - beyond the city centre, it is another story.

After months of trying, a BBC team managed to enter this dangerous world - centred on deprived streets and high-rise housing estates in the port city, which police do not enter lightly.

We found an environment where ruthless gangs lure vulnerable young people with promises of easy money, but end up trapping them in a world of drug dealing, brutality and exploitation.

We saw how gangs use social media to recruit hitmen and spoke to several young men caught up in the violence. From prison, one gang member accused of involvement in several murders explained how his "cold-bloodedness" had helped him rise through the ranks.

The city's most powerful gang, DZ Mafia, emerged victorious from a bloody turf war and is now one of the most feared criminal organisations in France.

DZ is the official internet country code for Algeria, where one of the gang's founders, a French-Algerian called Mehdi Laribi, was detained earlier this year under a French arrest warrant.

The criminal outfit rose to prominence in 2023, when it became the first French gang to capitalise on its notoriety by releasing video statements - using social media to market itself as a brand - says the head of the country's anti-drug trafficking unit, Dimitri Zoulas.

Its most recent statement came in July, when the mayor of a nearby town had to be placed in police protection, after intelligence suggested he was in danger of being targeted by the group.

In an online video, six masked men dressed in black stood behind a table - as one of them read a statement denying DZ Mafia's involvement.

France's expanding illegal drugs market - which has seen a surge in cocaine imports alongside high volumes of cannabis and synthetic drugs - has also helped the gang grow rapidly.

The number of cocaine users in France is expected soon to reach two million, says Zoulas, up from 600,000 in 2017. Drug smuggling across France generates €7bn (£5.9bn) a year, involving 200,000 people, he adds.

Many of those distributing the drugs are children and the authorities say the number of minors caught up in trafficking is increasing. During 2025, more than 10,000 children were involved in some way, according to official figures.

DZ Mafia is a prime example. To reach more customers, it needs more gang members - more children.

We have found it is now recruiting young people from across France - not just to sell drugs, but to carry out kidnap, torture and murder.

They are a generation seen as easy to corrupt, but also expendable, by the kingpins who typically control them from prison or overseas.

And, as police and judges warn, once these children enter Marseille's underworld, it is very hard to get them out.

Few know the human cost of Marseille's gangs like mother Karine Brouillard - who lives at the other end of France, almost as far from the Mediterranean coast as you can get.

Her son, Hugo, first ran away aged 15 - from his home in a village in the Nord department - after an argument with his family. He was picked up by police three days later, almost 1,000km (600 miles) away in Marseille, with money and cannabis on him. He was taken home.

But several years later, in 2023, Hugo planned to return south, telling his parents he had secured a holiday job at a restaurant near Marseille.

"He gave regular updates," Karine remembers. "He called me, everything was going well."

Three weeks later, a doctor called. Karine says she will never forget his words: "Your son arrived last night. He took a bullet to the head."

Police believe Hugo was brought for medical help from a gang-controlled area and suspect he was involved with one.

Our best way into Quartier Nord, where DZ Mafia wields power, is with the help of resident Fadella Ouidef, a 41-year-old mother-of-four who gives us a tour.

Thirty-seven seconds after entering one housing estate, we find ourselves cornered.

Car horns sound the moment Fadella's Peugeot passes a gang checkpoint - the teenagers manning the post immediately spot our camera. "Wait, stop filming," Fadella warns, as a grey 4x4 forces us to the side of the road.

"I'm making a report for my housing association," she tells the inquisitive driver. He eventually agrees to let us leave if we stop filming.

It is unnerving to see a non-police vehicle move so assertively and a relief to watch it leave.

"Lately, the gangs have been very aggressive," explains Fadella. "What we simply try to do is make sure our young people understand what's happening is wrong."

Fadella speaks to a wider fear among local families: that their children are enticed by huge sums of money to take a criminal path that robs them of their innocence.

Money is what led one young man to spend his teenage years with DZ Mafia.

In order for our interviewees to speak freely, or because of safety concerns, we have agreed to protect their identities.

Camil tells us he worked up the gang's ranks to "running security" in one area it controls.

The now 20-year-old, who claims to have left the group, is highly suspicious of our presence, but agrees to tell us how the gang recruits young members.

"They know how to get inside your head. Whatever you want, they give to you," he says. This can range from nice cars and spacious apartments, to drugs and prostitutes, he explains.

"You feel loyalty because of what they give you. You'll stay until the very end, until either death or prison."

Camil also gives a sobering assessment of what happens if the gang identifies a weakness in a recruit: "They'll exploit it. You're their bitch, it's over."

DZ Mafia member, Adam - not his real name - tells us he was part of a DZ Mafia hit squad when we speak to him in a Snapchat video call.

He is currently in prison awaiting trial, after being implicated in several murders.

"People noticed my determination, my cold-bloodedness and, without wanting to, I climbed up the ladder of the gang," says Adam. "It became my place, I had to roll with it."

During the chat, he agrees the killings he has been charged with were "quite shocking".

"Attempts in broad daylight, in traffic jams… it can range from going to hit a guy, slap him to taking him in front of his mother and burning him up in a car. I think I have good composure, I handle it fairly well."

We challenge Adam on whether he feels regret when carrying out such acts of brutality.

He says he is "feeling in-part guilty" but claims to have no regrets.

"If I hadn't done all of this, there are other people who would have done that in my place, and so on. I am just another brick in the wall," he says.

Like so many teenagers from Marseille, he knew large sums of money could be earned quickly in drug trafficking. Now in his twenties, he admits the environment he entered was a "trap".

At a so-called deal point in a social housing estate - sealed off and controlled by DZ Mafia - price lists for cocaine, hashish and marijuana are graffitied on a wall.

The estate acts as a natural fortress for drug dealers. With one major road in and out, they can control the flow of customers and see if the police are coming.

It is not uncommon for the sound of automatic gunfire to fill the night air in these areas.

After months of negotiations, a deal-point manager from a rival gang agrees to meet us where he works.

We enter the estate early in the morning, the birdsong and children walking to school providing a stark contrast to the industrial-scale criminal operation that takes place here.

"Joe" says he was making €3,000 (£2,500) a month when he was 13. Now he says that has risen to between €5,000 and €10,000 a month.

He seems to see his life path as pre-ordained, albeit a lucrative one.

We ask Joe if he thinks about the lives lost because of the violence carried out by his gang, but the 23-year-old has also long made peace with the pain and destruction drug trafficking can cause.

"It destroys people, but we all make our own choices," he shrugs.

The work that Joe's gang and DZ Mafia are doing represents a threat to national security, says Zoulas, of the anti-drug trafficking unit.

There are road accidents, as well as family violence, depressions, suicides and more than 700 overdoses each year, he says, "and it distorts the economy".

"We are heading towards a potential systemic breakdown of the criminal justice system."

Police have had success in Marseille and other cities against drug gangs.

Criminal operations are being frustrated, more kingpins arrested and drugs seized.

Since 2024, about 1,000 individuals associated with DZ Mafia have been arrested, and 600 incarcerated, police say.

But overall, it is a battle that is becoming more arduous, rather than easier.

As gangs seek to widen their operations, or replace members who have been arrested or killed, social media has become a potent recruitment tool - especially since the Covid pandemic, when many street-drug sales jumped online.

On social media, we found countless posts advertising jobs in Marseille for aspiring drivers, couriers and hitmen, often with glamourised AI-generated images.

Nets are also being cast wider, as it becomes harder to entice young people locally because they know more about what might happen to them.

The ads can reach teenagers in most corners of France - including Paris, Nantes and Lille - and serve as a powerful pull to Marseille, and the Quartier Nord, police say.

Online advertising has also changed the typical profile of someone who would join a gang's ranks, say law enforcement officials.

Now, it is often someone without a criminal past, but who has exploitable vulnerabilities, like having a difficult family life.

"These people are recruited by unscrupulous sponsors who send them into the lion's den," explains Thibaut Fontaine, the head of France's anti-organised-crime unit.

Their lack of criminal experience, he says, makes them easier to arrest quickly.

Karine still has no idea why her son, Hugo, was shot.

Asked what she would say to gang leaders recruiting children and young men in Marseille, she says: "They destroy families. Little sisters, little brothers, grandparents. But then, I don't think those people have a heart, really."

The restaurant where her son said he was going to work did exist, but staﬀ there told Karine they had never recruited anyone called Hugo.

The reason for his death almost certainly lies within Marseille's Quartier Nord.

Additional reporting by Marianne Baisnee, Lea Guedj and Paul Pradier

articles.title: Jensen Huang: Silicon Valley superstar engulfed by personal scandal
articles.summary: Once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech", Huang is mired in scandal after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang is one of the technology industry's most high-profile figures.

He rose to prominence as the business he leads - artificial intelligence (AI) chip giant Nvidia - became one of the world's most valuable companies.

As the face of the AI boom, Huang also became close to Donald Trump as the president pushed for the US to keep its dominance of the technology over China.

The 63-year-old who was once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech" and referred to as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan is now mired in scandal after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US.

He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.

Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia.

He has an estimated fortune of $155bn, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

"Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine - a biography on Huang, tells the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.

Huang has a famously close relationship with Trump. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Huang.

Trump said he had not spoken to the Nvidia boss since news of the investigation emerged.

"I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what's going on," Trump told reporters, adding that he had "done an amazing job for our country".

Huang has long found himself at the centre of US-China tensions. Trump has repeatedly said the two nations are in a race for dominance.

Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the fear is that if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities.

The US advantage is in large part because of US companies like Nvidia, working with producers like the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips.

Since 2022 the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security.

But it means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Jensen Huang once saying that Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero. In recent years Huang has engaged in a flurry of shuttle diplomacy, dashing between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way.

Sunday's revelations may explain why Huang has failed to bring home the biggest prize of all to Nvidia: the Trump administration's blessing to sell all but its most advanced chips to China .

Quarter after quarter of late, Nvidia has been locked out of that lucrative market. Despite his ostensible closeness to Trump, Huang has not managed to wrest this concession from the administration.

Huang founded Nvidia with fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993.

The company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games.

"In 2012 these machine learning neural net researchers started to use it for that purpose and Jensen immediately recognised that this was going to be a massive industry and the future of computing. He began to pour enormous amounts of resources into building what was essentially the AI hardware market," says Witt.

"Today when we think of that, we think of these giant data centres - none of that existed. There were no customers for the stuff he was building. In fact his first customer was Open AI at the time they had 30 people - he actually gave it to them, he donated it to them."

Nvidia is now worth some $4.5 trillion, making it one of the most valuable companies ever.

"The first real neural net of modern times on an Nvidia network was Alex Krizhevsky's Alexnet and they trained that on two Nvidia cards in Alex's bedroom. Now we do the same thing but we do it with 200,000 - 300,000 cards and instead of doing it in a bedroom we do it in a giant barn full of computers called a data centre," adds Witt.

"So when you think about a data centre buildout, when you hear the AI infrastructure buildout, Jensen runs a tollbooth. All of that goes through him. And it made his company at least temporarily, the most valuable company in the world."

Nvidia's board has announced a probe following reports by the New York Times that Huang had engaged in a romantic relationship with a woman believed by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy .

For now, though, Nvidia's board appears to have little appetite for removing Huang, saying in a statement on Sunday that they have "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team".

Sources tell the BBC his removal is unlikely because there is so much money at stake. There is also no clear successor to the 63-year old tech boss.

Huang met his wife Lori at Oregon State University, where she was also studying electrical engineering and was his lab partner.

They married in 1985, about eight years before he co-founded Nvidia, and have two children, Madison and Spencer.

He has credited Lori and Madison for making black leather jackets his signature style.

In 2007, the couple founded the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation.

The charitable fund has seen its assets surge in recent years, driven by the soaring value of Nvidia shares, and is estimated to be worth more than $9bn.

Its donations include tens of millions of dollars to engineering programmes at Oregon State and Stanford University.

"Jensen in my conversations with him and in other conversations has gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man. That's very important to him," says Witt.

"He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways. Both of his children work for Nvidia. Spencer and Maddison. The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad."

Huang for his part released a statement which said, " I was unfaithful to my wife . My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

US officials had concluded that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reports.

She was a top executive at Megaspeed, a data centre company based in Singapore. The firm had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia maintains was investigated and debunked.

Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking".

It remains unclear what information Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly passed to Beijing, how valuable it was, or when she is believed to have begun gathering intelligence.

Alice Huang did not respond to the paper's request for comment.

When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not.

"We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the US government would have notified us," an Nvidia spokesperson told the BBC.

Additional reporting by Ayeshea Perera in Singapore and Helen Davidson in Sydney
